source_caption:
To execute the highly kinetic “It’s the Hard-Knock Life” musical sequence, legendary director John Huston—a filmmaker previously known for gritty, hard-boiled classics like The Maltese Falcon rather than exuberant family musicals—demanded grueling, boot-camp-style rehearsals for the young cast. Choreographer Arlene Phillips designed the aggressive, stomping routine to incorporate heavy physical props, requiring the actresses to violently slam scrub brushes and toss metal buckets in perfect synchronization with the underlying track. The intense physical demands of the choreography, combined with the hazard of performing on deliberately wet, soapy floors, meant the children had to master stunt-level coordination to safely capture the visceral, rebellious energy of the orphanage floor-scrubbing scene.

Annie (1982), directed by John Huston, starring Aileen Quinn, Albert Finney, Carol Burnett, Tim Curry. A plucky, red-haired orphan is chosen to spend a week with a gruff billionaire, melting his heart and embarking on a high-stakes adventure to find her real parents while dodging the schemes of the cruel orphanage matron.

source_details.title: Annie
source_details.synopsis: Annie is a 1982 American musical comedy-drama film based on the 1977 Broadway musical of the same name by Charles Strouse, Martin Charnin and Thomas Meehan, which in turn is based on the Little Orphan Annie comic strip created by Harold Gray. Directed by John Huston and written by Carol Sobieski, it stars Albert Finney, Carol Burnett, Bernadette Peters, Ann Reinking, Tim Curry, Geoffrey Holder, Edward Herrmann, and Aileen Quinn in her film debut as the title character. It is the first film adaptation of the musical.
